neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The expansion over r explains how controlled auxiliary series recover the desired squarefree family and why absolute convergence of that outer expansion sets the accessible w-region and the previous error exponent.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to turn the cubic moments, indexed by fundamental discriminants, into the coefficients of a second Dirichlet variable w. This makes the family average accessible through the singularities of one two-variable analytic object rather than through termwise estimation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The span poses the m-th moment problem for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions, recalls the conjectural polynomial main term, and defines Z(s,w) as the sum over fundamental discriminants of L(s,chi_D)^3 divided by |D|^w.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a generating-series compression: dependence on the discriminant cutoff is exchanged for analytic structure in w. Poles in w can encode distinct power scales in a moment asymptotic, while s retains the L-function evaluation parameter.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Z(s,w) is the bridge from a discrete family of cubic central-value coefficients to complex-analytic continuation, residues, and eventually Mellin/Perron recovery of cutoff sums.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The definition alone proves neither continuation nor a moment asymptotic, and the surrounding conjectures are motivation rather than established consequences of this representation.
directed.uncertainty: The displayed formulas contain stray extraction glyphs, but the moment problem and the definition and role of Z(s,w) are readable.

supported: The span poses the moment problem, states the conjectural polynomial main term, and defines Z(s,w) by summing L(s,chi_D)^3 over fundamental discriminants with weight |D|^{-w}.
Treating the discriminant index as coefficients in a second Dirichlet variable is a genuine representation change, not a restatement.
inference: The new w-variable can reasonably be presented as a prospective analytic handle on cutoff moments.
unsupported_or_imported: The span does not mention singularities, residues, Mellin or Perron inversion, or establish that poles in w encode distinct asymptotic power scales.
The contrast with termwise estimation is not made in the frozen span.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The compression language is specific to the displayed construction, but the later analytic-payoff language outruns this introductory span.

missed_mechanism: The candidate should separate the actual construction in this span from analytic consequences proved or used only later.
revision_instructions: Keep the discriminant-to-w generating-series encoding and the explicit limitation that the definition proves no continuation or asymptotic; remove Perron/residue claims and either remove the singularity claim or phrase it only as a prospective strategy not established here.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Separate squarefree kernels and bad Euler factors
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Factoring each integer into a squarefree kernel and square part, then separating Euler factors at a chosen modulus, supplies the bookkeeping needed to move between primitive characters, imprimitive indices, and completed L-functions.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Packaging congruence and bad-prime corrections multiplicatively makes the final residue a comparison of Euler-product pole orders, turning many elaborate intermediate terms into zero unless all characters are principal.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The B, A, E, and R factors package recurring exceptional-prime algebra into multiplicative objects. Their value is compression: later divisor sums and residues can be recognized as Euler products instead of recomputed prime by prime.

directed.conceptual_reading: These definitions turn a collection of local correction rules into reusable multiplicative coordinates. The representation exposes factorization and pole-order comparisons while hiding lengthy casewise expansions inside named factors.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A_N and E_N bridge finite bad-prime corrections to the global completed series; R_M packages the global zeta quotient that later appears as a residue.
